messages.subject: Multi-year, multi-species N-mix stuck initializing
parts:
Hi all,

Thanks for this excellent package! I'm relatively new to it and have a question on options for speeding up a multi-species, year-stratified N-mixture model fit to robust design data. I ran the model overnight (12hrs), and it's still in the initializing stages (snippet below).

Are there recommendations for diagnosing slower steps or improving efficiency?

This is what the console shows currently:

Thank you!
Gates

messages.author: 0e6210fc31f1213e
messages.subject: Re: Multi-year, multi-species N-mix stuck initializing
parts:
Hi Gates,
In general (with my experience) the configuration step is the one that can take a prohibitive time and it would require to look at the number of dependencies for each node.
Although in your case it seems the compiling step is very long. I looked briefly at your model and the structure is fairly simple so I don't think the number of dependencies is an issue in your case.
However you have >17000 data and therefore >17000 likelihood calculations. I can imagine this could be the issue here, but maybe someone more used to this kind of model could confirm that.
Best,
Rémi

parts:
Hi all,

Thanks, Matt and Rémi, for the responses and suggestions! I really appreciate it. For a bit more context, if I fit a single species for all 33 years, it takes about a half-hour total. So, for 25 species, I thought it might take ~12.5 hours, but it appears to be taking upwards of 20 hours.

Matt: I've updated my code to use nimbleModel() with check and calculate set to F, rather than the single call to nimbleMCMC().  I'm re-running it now, and I think it should finish sometime this weekend.

Rémi: Yes, lots of data, which is somewhat unavoidable, but I could try to trim it down a little bit more. Just hoping there might be other options, too.

I've attached a small reproducible example (code and data) for 2 (of the 25) species for 2 (of the 33) years. It takes less than 2 minutes to run. In particular, I know that the code estimates latent abundances for site-years that aren't surveyed and, because of that, I get the warning "problem initializing stochastic node" for all of those missing site-years. Do I have to estimate latent abundances for the missing site years? Could this be slowing things down?

Thanks again!!

Best,
Gates

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Multi-year, multi-species N-mix stuck initializing
parts:
Hi Gates,

Another thing that can take a while is the configuration stage--the argument useConjugacy=FALSE while passing something to configureMCMC can also speed up model building a lot. 

Sampling the "unsampled" N's adds unnecessary calculations, but unless there are a lot of these, I doubt it's a substantial issue. Could use dynamic indexing to cut out some of these (i.e., only loop over the specific years sampled or the number of years sampled for a given site) if you wanted. Would reorder the looping for N to do this (e.g., site, nyears[site], species).

Cheers,

John

messages.subject: RE: Multi-year, multi-species N-mix stuck initializing
parts:
Dear Gates:

 

To avoid the warning "problem initializing stochastic node", try to add to inits:

 

lambda=array(1, c(n.data$nyears, n.data$nspecies))

 

Best regards,

José
